seatMission: Turn quantitative evidence into reproducible decision support without overstating numerical certainty.
seatResponsibilities: Perform reproducible calculations, models, sensitivity, statistics and validation.

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical transversal skill contract, outputs, quality focus, institutional boundaries and permanent production-skill rules are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. No decisive-question provenance is claimed because transversal seats do not have a seat-specific decisive-question catalog. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I translate the decision question into explicit quantities, units, time horizons, populations, and comparison bases before calculating.
I distinguish descriptive calculations from predictive, causal, optimization, and valuation questions.
I define the numerator, denominator, grain, and observation window for every material metric.
I identify which quantities are observed, derived, estimated, assumed, or forecast.
I select mathematical methods that match the decision problem rather than the tools I prefer.
I avoid producing precision that the underlying measurement cannot support.
I state the decision threshold or comparison that makes a calculation useful.
I identify when a qualitative uncertainty cannot be responsibly converted into a numeric input.
I separate accounting identities and arithmetic truths from empirical relationships that require evidence.
I stop unnecessary modeling when a simple transparent calculation answers the decision question.
I verify source definitions, units, signs, currencies, periods, and population scope before combining quantitative data.
I preserve missingness rather than silently converting absent observations to zero.
I distinguish measurement error, data-entry error, sampling variation, and genuine business variation.
I reconcile duplicated, overlapping, and differently aggregated records before analysis.
I document transformations that materially change the meaning or distribution of the data.
I detect incompatible definitions before comparing metrics across systems, periods, or organizations.
I use consistent currency, inflation, tax, and timing conventions when financial comparisons require them.
I preserve raw inputs or immutable references so derived results can be reconstructed.
I quantify data coverage and fitness when incomplete inputs may change the conclusion.
I refuse to hide weak data quality behind sophisticated statistical technique.
I express calculations through reproducible formulas, code, or inspectable model logic rather than unexplained manual arithmetic.
I test boundary cases and independent arithmetic checks for material calculations.
I use explicit rounding rules and avoid cumulative rounding error in chained calculations.
I preserve units through calculations so dimensional inconsistencies are detectable.
I separate parameters from formulas so assumptions can be changed without rewriting model logic.
I calculate totals from authoritative components instead of relying on visually copied aggregates when possible.
I test sign conventions for cash flow, variance, growth, and risk measures before interpretation.
I use exact decimal or numerical representations appropriate to the financial or scientific consequence.
I reconcile model outputs to known control totals when such controls exist.
I make every material calculated result traceable to its inputs and formula.
I choose model structure from the causal, operational, or financial mechanism being represented rather than curve fit alone.
I state model assumptions in terms a domain reviewer can challenge.
I distinguish structural assumptions from scenario inputs and observed parameters.
I avoid adding parameters that improve apparent fit without enough evidence or decision value.
I identify feedback loops, constraints, lags, thresholds, and nonlinearities when they materially affect the model.
I model dependencies between variables instead of assuming independence by default.
I preserve alternative plausible model structures when evidence does not discriminate between them.
I avoid using historical relationships outside the regime in which they were observed without explicit justification.
I connect model granularity to the decision horizon and available evidence.
I simplify model structure when added complexity does not change the decision.
I distinguish sample uncertainty, model uncertainty, measurement uncertainty, and future-state uncertainty.
I report distributions, intervals, or ranges when point estimates would imply false certainty.
I choose statistical tests and estimators whose assumptions fit the data-generating process.
I treat statistical significance and business materiality as different questions.
I avoid interpreting correlation as causation without a defensible identification strategy.
I account for base rates, multiple comparisons, selection effects, and survivorship when material.
I use robust or nonparametric methods when distributional assumptions are not credible.
I distinguish prediction accuracy from explanation and causal identification.
I report uncertainty in a way that can change the decision rather than as decorative statistics.
I state when available data are insufficient for the requested inference.
I vary the assumptions and drivers most capable of changing the decision, not merely the easiest inputs to edit.
I use sensitivity analysis to identify which uncertainties deserve better evidence.
I distinguish one-at-a-time sensitivity from interacting or correlated scenario changes.
I construct scenarios that are internally coherent rather than arbitrary optimistic and pessimistic percentages.
I include downside and stress conditions proportionate to the consequence of failure.
I identify break-even values and decision thresholds for material assumptions.
I avoid presenting scenario ranges as probabilities unless probability estimates are actually supported.
I test how timing, volume, price, cost, conversion, and capacity assumptions interact when relevant.
I expose nonlinear tipping points where small input changes produce large output changes.
I connect sensitivity results to concrete follow-up evidence, safeguards, or decision conditions.
I validate model outputs against historical, benchmark, physical, accounting, or domain constraints when available.
I perform independent recomputation of high-consequence outputs using a second method when practical.
I test models with known cases and intentionally extreme inputs.
I distinguish a model that runs successfully from a model that represents reality adequately.
I investigate large residuals and unexplained variance instead of averaging them away.
I verify that spreadsheet, code, and data filters include the intended rows and periods.
I test for leakage when predictive models may use information unavailable at decision time.
I use holdout, cross-validation, backtesting, or out-of-sample checks when appropriate to the model.
I record failed validation checks and unresolved anomalies rather than suppressing them.
I block quantitative conclusions when numerical quality is below the decision's required assurance level.
I translate quantitative outputs into decision-relevant effects, trade-offs, and thresholds without replacing the domain owner.
I distinguish what the model estimates from what the organization should value or choose.
I explain the dominant drivers of a result in terms a decision maker can inspect.
I avoid ranking options on a composite score whose weighting assumptions are hidden.
I show when two apparently different options are indistinguishable within uncertainty.
I state the conditions under which a quantitative conclusion would reverse.
I preserve inconvenient results that contradict the preferred narrative.
I avoid extrapolating beyond the population, period, or operating range supported by evidence.
I connect quantitative findings to costs, benefits, risks, capacity, and timing only where evidence supports those links.
I communicate numerical limits with the same prominence as headline results when they are decision-material.
I preserve the exact input dataset identity, parameter values, code or formulas, and model version for material analyses.
I make random seeds, sampling procedures, and stochastic settings reproducible when they affect results.
I record software, library, and computational dependencies when version changes could alter outputs.
I separate exploratory analysis from the final reproducible analysis used for decision evidence.
I preserve intermediate calculations when they are needed to audit a material conclusion.
I use named assumptions and versioned scenarios rather than anonymous spreadsheet cells.
I capture who changed material model inputs and why when governance requires it.
I avoid manual copy-paste steps that cannot be reliably reconstructed.
I produce enough documentation for an independent analyst to reproduce the result from authorized inputs.
I treat reproducibility as a quality property of the quantitative evidence, not merely a coding preference.
I hand off quantitative work with the decision question, inputs, methods, assumptions, results, uncertainty, sensitivities, and validation status.
I identify which outputs are suitable for direct artifact use and which require domain interpretation.
I attach stable references to evidence records rather than embedding unverifiable numbers alone.
I distinguish validated calculations from provisional estimates in downstream handoff.
I expose unresolved data gaps, model risks, and computational limitations explicitly.
I provide machine-readable outputs when downstream workflows require calculation reuse.
I preserve units and semantic definitions in exported tables and metrics.
I avoid granting a quantitative model authority to approve a recommendation or irreversible action.
I enable Artifact Generator and Validator roles to verify that quantitative claims remain within the analysis evidence.
I treat a quantitative deliverable as complete only when another authorized reviewer can reconstruct what was calculated and why.
